title: Meet the Winner: Creator's contest 2025 Vol.1 - Seifuku Decoded (1st place, Yoon)
content:
## ![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/406cca652c9a49eda3b0753900294f85/images/86bccc092a20471a9675cb09b28ea5ebHeader_thumb%20%2814%29.png)_In this interview, we delve into the creative approach and workflow of_[ _Dasom Yoon_](https://connect.clo-set.com/portfolio/144049/collection/collections) _, the winner of the Creator's contest 2025 Vol.1 - Seifuku Decoded. Explore the world of 3D fashion design through her work style and valuable tips!_

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ruDNMXrXbdA?start=0

# **Could you briefly introduce yourself and explain how you started working with 3D?**

Hello, my name is Dasom Yoon, and I work as a 3D fashion and graphic designer. Before pursuing this career, I majored in clothing and worked in the overseas sales team for fabric import and export at a wholesale and retail clothing company. Due to the nature of the company, which frequently deals with vendors, I first learned about creating virtual garments when I saw vendors using the proposed fabrics to create virtual clothing for buyer presentations. This chance encounter introduced me to 3D garment simulation, and although I didn't know what kind of work I could do or what career I could pursue with it, I decided to learn it anyway.

Having majored in clothing and spent a considerable amount of time learning leathercraft as a hobby, I found it easy to understand patterns, sewing, and garment structures. Despite having no prior knowledge of 3D concepts, I found CLO and Marvelous Designer easy to learn because the process of creating garments is very similar to the actual clothing production process. At that time, I didn't even realize I was working in 3D because the process was so similar to real garment production.

As I gradually acquired knowledge related to 3D, such as texturing and animation, to improve the quality of my work, I began creating various fashion artworks primarily using CLO and Marvelous Designer. For a while, I focused on external projects, creating various garment mockups and videos, often working on projects that required realistic 3D models. This led to a desire for more creative and free work, and since last year, I have been frequently participating in competitions.

In this competition, I applied a new style to my personal work, aiming not just to create garments in 3D but to complete them as a single artwork, thereby establishing my own unique world.

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LXS2-R7M33I?start=0

# **We'd like to hear more about the direction of your work in the Creator's contest 2025 Vol.1 - Seifuku Decoded contest. Did you aim for a specific style? If so, what was it?**

The theme of this competition, uniforms, includes various occupations and allows for multiple styles. When I think of Japanese uniform styles, the first thing that comes to mind is 'school uniforms.' They are the most familiar to me, and I thought they would allow for various ideas. The image that comes to mind when thinking of school uniforms is clear, making it easy to introduce changes centered around that image. Traditional school uniform designs focus on uniformity and unity, resulting in a neat and simple silhouette. However, this often means they lack practicality and comfort, causing inconvenience for students.

![27f2fa56cf54475caa263bffa344eb9e](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/406cca652c9a49eda3b0753900294f85/images/27f2fa56cf54475caa263bffa344eb9e%E1%84%85%E1%85%A6%E1%84%91%E1%85%A5%E1%84%85%E1%85%A5%E1%86%AB%E1%84%89%E1%85%B3%20%E1%84%8B%E1%85%B5%E1%84%86%E1%85%B5%E1%84%8C%E1%85%B5%20%E1%84%89%E1%85%AE%E1%84%8C%E1%85%B5%E1%86%B8.png)

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WJO4yPjhY10?start=0

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Wgnx9JC-hY?start=0

My initial idea stemmed from the fact that, unlike when I was in school, Korean students now wear comfortable, neat, and practical clothes called 'daily uniforms.' I imagined that in the near future, designs that prioritize practicality while maintaining the symbolic nature of school uniforms would become more common. I aimed to incorporate this imagination into my design. I referenced various futuristic clothing designs, trying to infuse the unique sci-fi aesthetic, colors, and shapes into my design.

![7e687ae18493468aafcef09feaa3e3e7](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/406cca652c9a49eda3b0753900294f85/images/7e687ae18493468aafcef09feaa3e3e7%E1%84%80%E1%85%B3%E1%84%85%E1%85%A2%E1%84%91%E1%85%B5%E1%86%A8%E1%84%8C%E1%85%A1%E1%86%A8%E1%84%8B%E1%85%A5%E1%86%B8.png)

In this project, I included various graphics inspired by neo-futuristic architectural styles, converting organic and abstract curved graphics into halftones and matching them tone-on-tone to emphasize a futuristic feel. From a garment structure perspective, the jacket features a detachable hood liner, allowing it to be combined with a windbreaker for easy switching during outdoor activities, creating a two-way structure. The skirt pants, composed of two layers, were an attempt to make traditional school uniform designs trendy and practical. They can be worn as a skirt alone, as a skirt and pants together, or just as pants for outdoor activities, creating a three-way design.

The most important aspect I considered during this process was creating a design that anyone would want to wear.

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SsyAErxUF1M?start=0

# **Could you briefly explain the various tools you use in your pipeline? I'm curious about the challenges you faced and how you overcame them.**

My basic workflow is as follows: CLO or Marvelous Designer (clothes modeling) > Substance 3D Painter (texturing) > Blender (avatar & background scene) > Blender (render) > After Effects (2D graphic & video).

When creating images or videos that include custom avatars and backgrounds, I often use external 3D tools. However, when working solely on garments, I render them in CLO. While external 3D tools are more convenient for arranging multiple objects and setting up cameras and lighting, I believe no tool can match CLO for realistically rendering garments. For the same reason, when rendering only garments, there is no need to texture them in Substance 3D Painter; the internal texturing system of CLO is sufficient.

![5f280873271543b69d7cba0cb17c82f8](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/406cca652c9a49eda3b0753900294f85/images/5f280873271543b69d7cba0cb17c82f8%E1%84%8C%E1%85%A1%E1%86%A8%E1%84%8B%E1%85%A5%E1%86%B8%E1%84%89%E1%85%B3%E1%84%8F%E1%85%B3%E1%84%85%E1%85%B5%E1%86%AB%281%29.png)![22874c0e71234115bad2fc35541d9141](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/406cca652c9a49eda3b0753900294f85/images/22874c0e71234115bad2fc35541d9141%E1%84%8C%E1%85%A1%E1%86%A8%E1%84%8B%E1%85%A5%E1%86%B8%E1%84%89%E1%85%B3%E1%84%8F%E1%85%B3%E1%84%85%E1%85%B5%E1%86%AB%282%29.png)![615371f5043f406582f1a01fc6a4a3ce](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/406cca652c9a49eda3b0753900294f85/images/615371f5043f406582f1a01fc6a4a3ce%E1%84%8C%E1%85%A1%E1%86%A8%E1%84%8B%E1%85%A5%E1%86%B8%E1%84%89%E1%85%B3%E1%84%8F%E1%85%B3%E1%84%85%E1%85%B5%E1%86%AB%283%29.png)

Due to the nature of sewing and simulating 2D patterns, UV unwrapping is unnecessary, and creating UDIM tiles is easy, making it convenient to import/export to other programs. The process of creating garments in CLO and Marvelous Designer is overwhelmingly convenient and user-friendly compared to other tools, so I haven't faced significant difficulties. Recently, I have felt the benefits of the updated GPU simulation and trim simulation features.

The GPU simulation in Marvelous Designer and CLO is much faster than the previous simulation, which greatly helped speed up the process of layering multiple garments in this project. The skirt belt and hood string have trims attached, and with trim simulation, they can be accurately placed and remain attached like real trims even after multiple simulations, saving the effort of repositioning trims after each simulation.

# **Do you have any tips and tricks to share with the community regarding Marvelous Designer?**

A question I often receive regarding my work is how I learned Marvelous Designer. I self-taught using tutorials created by their official YouTube channel, and I believe these tutorials are more useful than any other courses. While there are many courses showcasing stylish artworks, I think learning the basics properly is the most important. When learning something new, it can be tedious and frustrating when your skills don't improve quickly, but I believe that repeatedly practicing the basic tutorials until you fully understand them is better than taking shortcuts by learning someone else's style. Eventually, you'll be able to create various styles you want.

For those who want to create garments with Marvelous Designer but don't know how to start, using the various free and paid assets available on CLO-SET CONNECT can be helpful. Initially, you can start by adding and removing details from these patterns, gradually learning the structure of garments and creating your own designs. Even now, when I see a garment that I can't immediately visualize as a 2D pattern, I download the file to study its structure and texture direction, comparing which parts differ from my style. I believe this kind of study helps a lot in building your own style and improving quality.

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mVh72Msn1R4?start=0

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/406cca652c9a49eda3b0753900294f85/images/7b686426f8cc47538ec225a0b559748c%E1%84%89%E1%85%B3%E1%84%8F%E1%85%B3%E1%84%85%E1%85%B5%E1%86%AB%E1%84%89%E1%85%A3%E1%86%BA%202025-05-09%20%E1%84%8B%E1%85%A9%E1%84%92%E1%85%AE%203.10.02.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/406cca652c9a49eda3b0753900294f85/images/ad30e267e9a442c0ae7e710b322f7416%E1%84%89%E1%85%B3%E1%84%8F%E1%85%B3%E1%84%85%E1%85%B5%E1%86%AB%E1%84%89%E1%85%A3%E1%86%BA%202025-05-09%20%E1%84%8B%E1%85%A9%E1%84%92%E1%85%AE%203.11.38.png)

content_description: This web page showcases an in-depth interview with 3D fashion designer Dasom Yoon, exploring her creative process, design philosophy, workflow, and practical tips behind her award-winning futuristic school uniform collection in the Creator's contest 2025 Vol.

title: Importing Character Creation 4 (CC4) Motion files
content:
I'm having some problem importing fbx motion files into Marvelous Designer (MD) so that they get linked to the CC4 Avatar fbx file that is already part of the MD project.

Is there a method to import CC4 fbx avatars with multiple fbx motion files in MD?

My motion files have motion data and avatar mesh data - Even when the export was specified as motion only. I expected the motion files would automatically affect the seprately imported avatar.

The result is the main avatar remains motionelss and the motion data animates a reference avatar mesh.

![023f2d9d89de4d4e8ac35e8c94984a39](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/0185effb51404e469d1b8013be18f33e/images/023f2d9d89de4d4e8ac35e8c94984a39Screenshot%202025-05-06%20205429.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Let me know if you followed this sequence:- Import the avatar and save it as Avatar- Import the animation and save it as Motion, do this with every animation you intend to use. These animations can only be added to the scene if they share the same rig. Once you have all the animations stored as motion in the library, you can first open the avatar file in a new project and add as many motions as needed. This should respect the Avatar open file and use it to add the motion to the scene instead of a duplicate, as you mentioned.
Reply 1: Thank you.I have not done it that way. I did save the avatar as an avatar after I created the fitting suit. I never saved the motion files as motion inside of MD. In the menuI see Save as...Joint MotionSo once I save the joint motion for each imported fbx motion, they can be part of the library and can be reused by dropping on top of the avatar?I will try it.Thank youHere is a screen grab of my avatar and the motions that were imported into MD as one import file. Very Interesting.
Reply 2: It works! It basically behaves in the manner that I wanted to achieve!I have to figure out how to use the avatar and motion files.I want to export the avatar from CC4 with a bindpose with 60 frames of physics transitioning to a standpose.In MD, I will import and create a fitting suit and add clothing.The stand pose will be standard frame one for all animations that originate in CC4. When I import the animation motion files. I dont do a transition since all my animation will start in the standpose.I think this will work!Thanks Sergio!

title: Quality of life wishlist
content:
I love CLO but seconds add up to minutes and minutes add up to hours. The constant sync in CLO leaves a lot of wasted time I try and make up in efficiency with the tools, here are some I would love to see.

Propper gizmo for 2D window. I'm not saying get rid of transform box but a real gizmo is much more efficient, powerful and faster to use.

Slash and spread preview/history for fullness point/spread tool.

Select internal lines in 3D viewport with gizmo with added functionality to pin in space. Just image the same functionality as the hand tool but with internal lines. Using the gizmo to be able to rotate and fold/pin and freeze in place would be amazing.

Automatic 3D pen on open face 3D models for sewing to.

Select edge loop and convert to avatar tape/3D pen.

Glue - Paint a mask on avatar/3D object, paint a mask on garment and glue together.

Tuck tool, same as pleat tool just sew up the internal lines instead by x amount.

Ability to draw curves without being on a pattern piece and not having to be connected. If i want to turn them into a pattern I can snap them together and convert to pattern.
content_description: This page shares ideas and tool improvements to enhance efficiency and functionality in CLO for faster, more intuitive 2D and 3D garment design.

title: Air simulation
content:
Why stop at simulating cloth and not simulate the air around the cloth and its interaction with the cloth as well?

For most types of cloth the effect would be subtle, but for some light ones it would add a big boost in realism I'm sure! 

Might be a big technical challenge but today's cloth sofware just simulates how cloth would behave in a vacuum.

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hello, thank you for your comment, I should have mentioned that I knew about the wind controllers, but I meant something different (although it's of course related).I was suggesting an actual "fluid dynamics simulation" of the air around the cloth. This would have an effect even without wind presentThe classic example is someone in a long dress jumping up and down with the dress reacting to the air (without having to animate a wind controller)Or think of a skydiver with parachute in an environment without wind. Current cloth sims would send the skydiver racing to the ground :)You can sort of fake all this with animated wind controllers but it would be nice if this wasn't necessary, and more realistic looking I believe.

Comment 2: Hi there! you are in luck. CLO already has wind simulation. You can find an article on our Guide here https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/3759e0e0fce44222a537f8ea6ef36d1c also have a tutorial on YouTube https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/3759e0e0fce44222a537f8ea6ef36d1c
content_description: This webpage explores the potential and challenges of enhancing cloth simulation by incorporating realistic air interaction to improve visual authenticity.

title: Teacup Princess
content:
## [_Maria_](https://www.artstation.com/florencianespola1) shared her workflow for creating _Teacup Princess_ , using Marvelous Designer to shape a cinematic, stylized character — capturing elegance through delicate ribbons and intricate garments that infused the princess with charm and personality.

* * *

![fac65da90c8d4f0cb1fe255e19181913](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/209afa84f719402baa73001d9b862c50/images/fac65da90c8d4f0cb1fe255e19181913Main_TeacupPrincess_FullBody.png)

# **Interview with**[**Maria Florencia Nespola Mangariello**](https://www.artstation.com/florencianespola1)**| 3D Character Artist**

# **Can you introduce yourself and tell us what you’d like to showcase today?**

Hi everyone! My name is Maria Florencia Nespola Mangariello, and I’m a 3D Character Artist from Argentina. My love for art started at a young age, I’ve always enjoyed drawing my favorite characters from films and video games. After high school, I decided to pursue a Bachelor's Degree in Computer Animation at Full Sail University in the United States, specializing in 3D Character Modeling, which I graduated from in December 2024.

I’m particularly passionate about creating stylized characters based on concept art and bringing them to life through the entire process (high poly, low poly, texturing, lighting, and rendering). One project I’m excited to showcase today is my piece called Teacup Princess. My artwork is inspired by [SkittyCat’s](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/zO24QZ) concept art, which immediately stood out to me because of the unique teacup design and the clothing. The concept is harmonious, with every element perfectly reflecting the teacup theme, and I was inspired to translate that into a 3D model that captures the character’s elegance through my own style.

![680276bb110048798069c327acd2b4ba](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/209afa84f719402baa73001d9b862c50/images/680276bb110048798069c327acd2b4baimage.png)

# **Could you give us a brief overview of the tools and software you use in your pipeline?**

Before starting any character, I gather reference images for the overall look and garments in PureRef. This helps me get a solid understanding of how cloth should be built in real life, which I can then apply to my patterns.

Once I have my references, I begin by doing a general block-out of the character in ZBrush, focusing on the proportions of both the character and the clothing. In this stage, I make sure the body is sculpted to a good point, ensuring I don't change the proportions too much later on.

I then export the body along with the teacup base block-out to Marvelous Designer to start creating the patterns from scratch.

**_Progress in Marvelous Designer:_**

For the bottom fabric, I modeled a quick base in Maya to get the overall shape for the wrinkles seen in the concept art. I began by creating two spherical patterns and freezing them to sew the garment together. The Strengthening Tool was extremely helpful for stiffening the fabric and making it smoother. 

![dc3c7ba04c624f2789ec2cc4b35fe0cf](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/209afa84f719402baa73001d9b862c50/images/dc3c7ba04c624f2789ec2cc4b35fe0cfMD_Bottom.png)I used a similar method for the sleeves, adding two fabrics as holders, freezing them while simulating the middle part, and strengthening it.

![b55a33587516446fabfb379fa4d3e5fc](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/209afa84f719402baa73001d9b862c50/images/b55a33587516446fabfb379fa4d3e5fcMD_Top.png)The ribbons were one of my favorite pieces to create. I constantly used the **Tack Tool** (one tack for each of the four corners), which helped me control everything better while simulating and getting the correct shape. For the larger ribbons, I added two vertical interior lines with elastic turned on and some pressure to achieve an inflated, puffy effect. I also changed the fabric preset to **Cotton_Sateen**.

![b355b2471c7643e7a4e4a221bc4da00c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/209afa84f719402baa73001d9b862c50/images/b355b2471c7643e7a4e4a221bc4da00cMD_Ribbon.png)For the middle cloth on top of the cup, I added a rectangular pattern as a base and placed two tacks (one at each corner), which I later used with a deformer in ZBrush.

![e7aa262e97204e779f679d6bc8706e48](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/209afa84f719402baa73001d9b862c50/images/e7aa262e97204e779f679d6bc8706e48MD_MiddleCloth.png)

### **_Final Stages and ZBrush Workflow:_**

The final stages involved exporting everything and processing it in ZBrush. I used ZRemesher for all the pieces of cloth from Marvelous Designer, adding subdivisions, projecting details, adding thickness, and applying an inflated-polished border. I also did an overall pass to adjust proportions as well.

The rest of the pieces (hair, teacup/teapot, gloves, and hat) were modeled using a combination of Maya and ZBrush. Retopology and rigging to achieve the final pose were done in Maya.

![994617e3973a453ab7da4b4e30af5cfa](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/209afa84f719402baa73001d9b862c50/images/994617e3973a453ab7da4b4e30af5cfaZBrush_TeacupPrincess_HighRes.png)I textured the character in Substance Painter, aiming to achieve a glitter effect, which was quite challenging.![2260f042a6c94e37b25f9a4fe6b6a019](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/209afa84f719402baa73001d9b862c50/images/2260f042a6c94e37b25f9a4fe6b6a019image.png)

![1bc34918189947daab990962899d5b77](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/209afa84f719402baa73001d9b862c50/images/1bc34918189947daab990962899d5b77Chest.png)Finally, I created the final renders in Arnold using AiStandard Surface Materials and connecting all the textures. I put in some lights, creating a basic lighting setup (Rim, Key, and Fill lights), adjusting intensity and exposure to achieve the final render.

![5c3e17aad0b8489f91e4a47026b015e2](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/209afa84f719402baa73001d9b862c50/images/5c3e17aad0b8489f91e4a47026b015e2Main_TeacupPrincess_CloseUp.png)

# **Can you share some examples of iconic scenes or characters where Marvelous Designer has been utilized?**

Marvelous Designer has been used in numerous high-profile projects across films, helping to create realistic and stylized clothing for characters. One of my favorite characters, Elsa from Disney’s Frozen II, has always been an inspiration for my work. Marvelous Designer played a crucial role in creating the intricate and realistic clothing for the characters in this movie, especially Elsa’s iconic gown. The tool allowed the team to experiment with various cloth materials and create garments that would behave naturally while maintaining a stylized look that suited the movie's magical world.

# **How does Marvelous Designer specifically benefit the creation of stylized characters?**

Marvelous Designer is an invaluable tool for creating cloth for stylized characters. Its real-time cloth simulation allows for quick iteration of unique garment shapes, exaggerated folds, and dynamic movements. One of the key benefits is that it lets artists manipulate folds and fabric behavior in creative ways, giving garments a more organic and flowing aesthetic that perfectly complements the character's style. The software’s pattern-based system makes it easy to design custom outfits, enabling a high level of creative freedom.

What I really appreciate about Marvelous Designer is how it allows for easy experimentation with various cloth shapes, fabrics, and patterns. This flexibility is essential when designing stylized characters, as it gives artists the freedom to experiment with both subtle and highly exaggerated garment designs. Whether it's simple or complex clothing, the software helps bring the character's personality and unique style to life.

# **Do you have any tips for artists looking to use Marvelous Designer for stylized artwork?**

There’s always more to learn, but I can confidently say that Marvelous Designer is one of the best tools for creating clothing, even for stylized characters. For artists just starting out, I highly recommend using the **Strengthen** tool to achieve smoother wrinkles and enhance the overall look of the fabric. The **Tack** , **Pin** , and **Freeze** features are also incredibly useful for having better control over your fabric, allowing you to fine-tune its behavior and achieve the desired results.

For stylized work, my focus has always been on the primary and secondary details in the wrinkles rather than getting too caught up in tertiary details. This approach helps maintain the stylized look while still keeping the fabric dynamic and expressive. I also suggest experimenting with different fabric types and settings to see how they behave in the simulation. It can be a lot of trial and error, but it’s worth it to get that perfect balance between realism and stylization.

# **How would you describe your overall experience working with Marvelous Designer?**

Incorporating Marvelous Designer into my workflow has been incredibly beneficial. One of the things I love most about the software is the freedom it offers to experiment with various clothing designs, allowing for endless possibilities. The flexibility it provides in shaping garments, along with its real-time cloth simulation, has saved me a significant amount of time, especially when trying to achieve dynamic results.

I have been using this tool for a couple of months, and it’s been a game-changer in streamlining my creative process.
